findings.title: parseBody() breaks after c.req.formData() was already called
findings.suggested_fix: In parseFormData, short-circuit on an existing cache before reading bytes, mirroring validator.ts:115-116: `let formData: FormData; if (request instanceof HonoRequest && request.bodyCache.formData) { formData = await request.bodyCache.formData } else { const arrayBuffer = await (request as Request).arrayBuffer(); const formDataPromise = bufferToFormData(arrayBuffer, headers.get('Content-Type') || ''); if (request instanceof HonoRequest) { request.bodyCache.formData = formDataPromise as unknown as FormData } formData = await formDataPromise }`. Add tests in src/request.test.ts for `await req.formData()` followed by `await req.parseBody()` for both multipart and urlencoded bodies.
findings.first_evidence:
src/utils/body.ts:126-127 -- const arrayBuffer = await (request as Request).arrayBuffer()
  const formDataPromise = bufferToFormData(arrayBuffer, headers.get('Content-Type') || '')

residual_risks: Behavior was verified only on Node 24 (undici). parseBody no longer calls the runtime's native request.formData(); it reads arrayBuffer() and parses through new Response(...).formData(). Bun, Deno, Workers and Lambda runtime tests were not run (forbidden by the execution policy), so parity of that path on those runtimes is unconfirmed.
testing_gaps: No test covers the new cache write at src/utils/body.ts:130: parseBody() followed by c.req.formData() / c.req.text() / cloneRawRequest() on the same HonoRequest for a form body. A scratch run shows these work at head (cache keys become [arrayBuffer, formData]; text() now returns the original bytes), but nothing pins it.

findings.title: No test for formData()-then-parseBody(); order now regresses
findings.suggested_fix: In `parseFormData` (src/utils/body.ts), before the `arrayBuffer()` read, reuse an already cached FormData: `if (request instanceof HonoRequest && request.bodyCache.formData) { return convertFormDataToBodyData<T>(await request.bodyCache.formData, options) }`. Add tests to the `req.parseBody()` block in src/request.test.ts that build a `HonoRequest` with (a) a `FormData` body and (b) a `URLSearchParams` body, call `await req.formData()` first, then assert `await req.parseBody()` equals `{ foo: 'bar' }`.
findings.first_evidence: src/utils/body.ts:126 -- const arrayBuffer = await (request as Request).arrayBuffer()

findings.title: New parseBody formData cache branch has no asserting test
findings.suggested_fix: Extend 'should parse form data' in src/request.test.ts (line 368) with `expect((await req.formData()).get('foo')).toBe('bar')` after the `parseBody()` call, and add the same assertion for a `URLSearchParams` body with `Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded`.
findings.first_evidence: src/utils/body.ts:130 -- request.bodyCache.formData = formDataPromise as unknown as FormData

residual_risks: On Node v24.21.0 the platform already accepts mixed-case media types: native `Response.formData()` with `Multipart/Form-Data; boundary=sampleBoundary` and native `Request.formData()` with `Application/X-WWW-Form-Urlencoded` both parse without Hono's normalization. Whether the `bufferToFormData` lowercasing and the `request.formData()` -> `arrayBuffer()` rewrite are needed on Bun, Deno, workerd, or Lambda is unverified because runtime-tests could not be run in this review.

Callsite completeness is grep-only: the claim that no test exercises formData()-then-parseBody() or parseBody()-then-formData() on a form request rests on text search of src/ and runtime-tests/; no suite-level mutation run was performed.
testing_gaps: src/utils/buffer.test.ts 'Should parse mixed-case multipart/form-data media type while keeping the boundary' passes on Node without the src/utils/buffer.ts change (native Response.formData() parses the identical input), so it guards only against over-lowercasing the boundary, not against the media-type normalization being removed or turned into a no-op.

The two new mixed-case tests in src/utils/body.test.ts pass on Node with only the `parseBody` guard change plus the old `request.formData()` call, so no test in the main project demonstrates what the `arrayBuffer()` + `bufferToFormData` rewrite of `parseFormData` buys; the rewrite's cost (finding 1) is likewise untested.
parseBody on a HonoRequest after `c.req.text()` on a multipart body changed from throwing (base) to returning the parsed fields (head); no test records either behavior.

findings.title: parseBody after c.req.formData() reparses re-serialized body (CWE-436)
findings.suggested_fix: In `parseFormData` (src/utils/body.ts), reuse an existing cached FormData before touching the bytes, mirroring validator.ts:115-116: `if (request instanceof HonoRequest && request.bodyCache.formData) { return convertFormDataToBodyData<T>(await request.bodyCache.formData, options) }`, and only fall through to `arrayBuffer()` + `bufferToFormData()` when no FormData is cached. Add a test in src/request.test.ts that calls `req.formData()` then `req.parseBody()` for both urlencoded and multipart bodies.
findings.first_evidence:
src/utils/body.ts:126-127 -- const arrayBuffer = await (request as Request).arrayBuffer()
  const formDataPromise = bufferToFormData(arrayBuffer, headers.get('Content-Type') || '')

residual_risks: parseBody's new gate uses `split(';')[0].trim().toLowerCase()`; JS `trim()` strips more than HTTP whitespace (e.g. U+00A0, U+000B), so it accepts values the csrf middleware regex (`/^\b(application\/x-www-form-urlencoded|multipart\/form-data|text\/plain)\b/i`) does not treat as form submissions. On Node v24 this did not produce a CSRF bypass: such requests reach `Response.formData()`, which rejects the Content-Type, so the handler returns 500 instead of the previous `{}`; browsers also cannot send these values cross-site without a preflight. Not verified on Bun, Deno or workerd, whose `Response.formData()` MIME parsing may differ.

For HonoRequest, parseBody now keeps both the raw `arrayBuffer` and the parsed `formData` in `bodyCache` for the life of the request (previously only the FormData), roughly doubling retained memory for large multipart uploads on routes without the body-limit middleware. Not measured.

findings.title: parseBody() after c.req.formData() now throws or returns garbage
findings.suggested_fix: In parseFormData (src/utils/body.ts), reuse the cached FormData for a HonoRequest and set the cache before awaiting: `if (request instanceof HonoRequest) { const contentType = request.raw.headers.get('Content-Type') || ''; request.bodyCache.formData ??= request.arrayBuffer().then((buf) => bufferToFormData(buf, contentType)) as unknown as FormData; formData = await request.bodyCache.formData } else { formData = await bufferToFormData(await request.arrayBuffer(), request.headers.get('Content-Type') || '') }`. Verified on a scratch copy of the head sources: formData()->parseBody(), both concurrent orders, parseBody()->formData(), validator('form') in either order, cloneRawRequest after parseBody, and mixed-case urlencoded all return the correct fields. Add a regression test in src/request.test.ts for `await req.formData(); await req.parseBody()` with both multipart and urlencoded bodies.
findings.first_evidence: src/utils/body.ts:126 -- const arrayBuffer = await (request as Request).arrayBuffer()

residual_risks: parseBody() media-type matching went from prefix (`startsWith`) to exact equality on the part before `;` (src/utils/body.ts:104-106). Verified in a scratch run: a comma-joined duplicate header `application/x-www-form-urlencoded, application/x-www-form-urlencoded` returned {"a":"1"} at base and returns {} at head. Only malformed/duplicated Content-Type headers are affected, so this is noted rather than raised as a finding.

parseBody() no longer calls `request.formData()`; it calls `request.arrayBuffer()` and parses via `new Response(...).formData()` (src/utils/body.ts:126-127). The exported `hono/utils/body` parseBody now throws `request.arrayBuffer is not a function` for a request-like object that only implements `formData()`, and `formData` spies/mocks are bypassed (the PR had to drop `vi.spyOn(req, 'formData')` from src/utils/body.test.ts). In-repo callers (HonoRequest.parseBody, method-override) pass real Request objects and are unaffected; external consumers were not checked.

After parseBody(), `Object.keys(c.req.bodyCache)` is now ['arrayBuffer','formData'] instead of ['formData'], so later `c.req.text()/arrayBuffer()/blob()` and `cloneRawRequest()` return the original bytes rather than a re-serialized FormData. Verified as an improvement for the in-repo consumers (cloneRawRequest after parseBody failed for multipart and corrupted urlencoded at base, works at head), but third-party code reading the public `bodyCache` property sees a different shape.
Only Node 24 (undici) was exercised; the execution policy forbids Deno/Bun/Workers/Lambda runtime tests, so buffer-then-`Response.formData()` behaviour on those runtimes was not verified.
testing_gaps: No test covers body-cache ordering around parseBody() for form requests: validator('form') followed by `c.req.parseBody()`, and `c.req.parseBody()` followed by validator('form') (both pass at head in a scratch run, but nothing guards the new arrayBuffer-plus-formData cache shape).

findings.title: c.req.formData() before c.req.parseBody() now throws or returns garbage
findings.suggested_fix: In `parseFormData` (src/utils/body.ts), reuse the cached FormData and set the cache synchronously instead of always re-deriving from an ArrayBuffer. For a HonoRequest: `request.bodyCache.formData ??= request.arrayBuffer().then((buf) => bufferToFormData(buf, contentType)) as unknown as FormData; const formData = await request.bodyCache.formData`. For a plain Request keep `bufferToFormData(await request.arrayBuffer(), contentType)`. This mirrors the existing `if (c.req.bodyCache.formData)` guard at src/validator/validator.ts:115-116 and also closes the concurrent `Promise.all([c.req.parseBody(), c.req.formData()])` window. Add regression tests in src/request.test.ts for `formData()` then `parseBody()` with both multipart and urlencoded bodies. Assumption: the arrayBuffer route is wanted for runtimes whose native `Request.formData()` is case-sensitive; on Node 24 native `Request.formData()` already parses `Multipart/Form-Data`, so simply reverting to `await request.formData()` with only the new media-type guard is an alternative if that holds on every supported runtime.
findings.first_evidence:
src/utils/body.ts:126-127 -- const arrayBuffer = await (request as Request).arrayBuffer()
  const formDataPromise = bufferToFormData(arrayBuffer, headers.get('Content-Type') || '')

residual_risks: Repeated `c.req.parseBody()` calls on one request no longer share a parse: each call re-parses the cached ArrayBuffer and replaces `bodyCache.formData`, so two calls return different `File` instances (scratch run: head `a.f === b.f` is false, base true), and the request now keeps both the raw ArrayBuffer and the parsed FormData alive (`bodyCache` keys `arrayBuffer,formData` vs `formData` at base). Memory and CPU cost for large multipart uploads was not measured.

`src/middleware/method-override/index.ts:74` and `:92` still match Content-Type with case-sensitive `startsWith('multipart/form-data')` / `startsWith('application/x-www-form-urlencoded')`. A `Multipart/Form-Data` request carrying `_method=DELETE` is still not overridden; after this change the un-overridden POST handler's `parseBody()` now returns the form (including `_method`) instead of `{}`. Outside the issue's stated scope, not changed by the diff.

`parseBody` matching changed from prefix to exact media type: a comma-joined duplicate header value `application/x-www-form-urlencoded, application/x-www-form-urlencoded` now returns `{}` where base parsed the fields on Node 24 (scratch run), and values such as `multipart/form-data-foo` now return `{}` instead of throwing. Whether any supported adapter produces comma-joined Content-Type values was not checked.
All runtime behaviour was verified on Node v24.21.0 (undici) only; Bun, Deno, and Workers were not run (excluded by the execution policy).
testing_gaps: The new mixed-case tests in src/utils/body.test.ts pass a plain `Request` (`createRequest` returns `new Request(...)`), so the new HonoRequest-only branch in `parseFormData` (`request.bodyCache.formData = formDataPromise`) is never exercised with a mixed-case Content-Type through `c.req.parseBody()`; a scratch run shows it works today (`Multipart/Form-Data` -> `{message: 'hello'}`, then `c.req.formData()` returns the same entry).

findings.title: parseBody() re-derives form data from bytes, ignoring a cached FormData
findings.suggested_fix: Reuse `request.bodyCache.formData` when a HonoRequest already has it instead of always calling `arrayBuffer()` and re-parsing against the original Content-Type header.
